chapter.title: A New Home
chapter.note: Rebuilt on 6 November 2026 at flowchart-node level from the PowerPyx 100% chart (30 nodes) and the Fandom wiki (chapter page, transcript, Relationship Stat). WELCOME HOME → JOIN TODD → [ CLEAN FIRST FLOOR ] → TAKE OUT TRASH → ASK TO GO UPSTAIRS → GO UPSTAIRS → [ CLEAN SECOND FLOOR ] → TALK WITH ALICE → FINISHED CLEANING, the only ending. Every other node is optional: two magazines (four covers), the dishes, the backyard and its talk, the rewash that finds Red Ice and enrages Todd, the vacuum, disturbing Todd, the toilet, the bathroom, the pills that reveal the gun (unlock), Alice’s window and its way down (unlock), the key at least at Neutral, and Alice’s box. No probability, public-opinion or instability change; Alice starts Distant and has nine small increases and one decrease (asking about her mother). Cross-chapter: the gun (Stormy Night, Fugitives), the window (Stormy Night), the box and its family photo (Battle for Detroit), the book and the Red Ice (Zlatko). Researched in docs/research/chapters/ch04-a-new-home.md. Story 1.7.0: the dialogue options show the game’s button labels (GAME, BACKYARD, WEATHER, SCHOOL, TOY, FACTUAL, FRIENDLY, DIPLOMATIC, NAME KARA, INTERESTS?, SEEM QUIET, MOTHER?, LEAVE ALONE), with the spoken line in the outcome.

decisions.title: Welcome Home (checkpoint) and Join Todd
decisions.context: Todd brings Kara home: “You’ve been gone for two weeks and the place is a mess.” Her duties are housework, washing, meals and looking after Alice (“Homework, bath, all that crap”). Alice appears on the stairs with a toy. “Get started down here, then you do upstairs.”

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: The start node and checkpoint. Optional looks at the bridge and the excavator are not on the chart.

decisions.gate: Chapter start, after Shades of Color.
decisions.note: Chart nodes WELCOME HOME (checkpoint) and JOIN TODD. No icon on either.

benchmark.note: A narrated event with a single Continue, quoting the transcript. Two facts go to Kara’s knowledge; no stat change. Alice’s age is no longer given. Story 1.9.7: Todd says “gone for two weeks, so the place is a mess” as in the string table (MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough, g_DQfghTbLg 15:15).

decisions.title: Read the dining-table magazine
decisions.context: A magazine with two covers on the dining table, among the dirty dishes.

options.label: READ “ANDROID POWER!”
options.effect: All Sports: an android pitcher breaks 120 mph; androids dominate baseball; fans disenchanted.

options.label: READ “CONNECTING THE DOTS”
options.effect: Century: the SubTube runs New York to Los Angeles in under two hours; California prices up 64%; “First Detroit takes our jobs, then New York takes our homes?”

decisions.gate: Optional, any time on the first floor, also after reporting to Todd.
decisions.note: Two optional chart nodes from one branch origin. No public-opinion effect.

benchmark.note: A media scene before the chores: read either, both or neither. Facts go to Kara’s knowledge; no stat change.

decisions.title: Take out trash
decisions.context: The only urgent first-floor task: collect the trash in the kitchen, on the counter and on the coffee table and carry the bags out. Todd takes a phone call (“Yeah, yeah I’ll bring it tomorrow. Yes, same place”); back inside he tears the shelf apart for his Red Ice and smokes it on the couch.
decisions.note: Chart node on the line leaving [ CLEAN FIRST FLOOR ]. Todd’s hunt for Red Ice always follows; the phone call “happens by performing a task”.

benchmark.note: An option of the repeatable first-floor scene; going upstairs requires it. Kara learns the phone call and the Red Ice hunt.

decisions.title: Wash dishes
decisions.context: The dishwasher is broken (missing component #573BV; Kara orders it). Kara washes by hand; Alice comes in and watches her. Todd then demands a cold beer.

options.label: WASH DISHES
options.effect: Alice relationship up (“Washing the dishes ↑”). BRING TODD A BEER follows (mandatory, not a chart node).

options.label: Leave them
options.effect: The dishes and the magazine are still on the table at the end.

decisions.note: Small increase in the wiki’s Relationship Changes.

benchmark.note: Hub option, Alice +1; the beer is part of the outcome. The ending notes whether the table is clear.

decisions.title: Check backyard
decisions.context: Kara goes out the back door and takes the laundry off the line; Alice follows and sits on a tire.

options.label: CHECK BACKYARD
options.effect: Enables the backyard talk and REWASH CLOTHES.

decisions.note: Chart node; objective TAKE DOWN LAUNDRY.

benchmark.note: Hub option; the yard talk is offered right after it, the rewash any time after it.

decisions.title: Talk with Alice (backyard)
decisions.context: Two menus, each GAME, BACKYARD, WEATHER, SCHOOL, minus the line already said. Alice stays silent.

options.label: GAME
options.effect: Alice up: “Offering to play a game with Alice when talking to her in the backyard ↑”.

options.label: BACKYARD
options.effect: Alice up: “Asking Alice about the garden when talking to her in the backyard ↑”.

decisions.gate: Optional, right after taking down the laundry.
decisions.note: Chart node TALK WITH ALICE (speech bubble, first floor). Whether the indoor TOY talk also lights it is unclear.

benchmark.note: A hub option that cuts into two dialogue scenes (the second drops the first pick) and returns to the first floor. At most +2. Options show the game’s labels GAME, BACKYARD, WEATHER, SCHOOL.

decisions.title: Rewash clothes, find Red Ice, enrage Todd
decisions.context: Kara rewashes the laundry, finds Red Ice hidden in the Blue Splash detergent and scans it; Todd pins her to the wall: “You shouldn’t mess around with my stuff! It makes me nervous!” Alice watches.

options.label: REWASH CLOTHES
options.effect: Always followed by FIND RED ICE and ENRAGE TODD (triangle events). Zlatko: “Recall Todd’s Red Ice Pipe (If Kara washed Todd’s clothes in A New Home)”.

decisions.note: Three chart nodes in a chain; no relationship change in the transcript.

benchmark.note: One hub option for the chain; the fact is kept for Zlatko (downstairs.rewash).

decisions.title: Activate vacuum
decisions.context: The vacuum robot left of the TV; Alice plays with it and Todd shouts at her (“Why is she always pushin’ me?”).
decisions.note: Chart node.

benchmark.note: Hub option, no stat change.

decisions.title: Disturb Todd
decisions.context: Kara stands in front of the TV while Todd watches hockey: “Outta the way for fuck sake!”
decisions.note: Chart node, drawn grey/white on the photographed chart (unexplained).

benchmark.note: Hub option, no stat change.

decisions.title: Compliment Alice’s toy (not a chart node)
decisions.context: Kara kneels by Alice: “That’s a pretty toy! What’s it’s name?”

options.label: TOY
options.effect: Alice up: “Complimenting her teddy after cleaning the first floor of the house ↑”.

decisions.gate: Optional; the transcript and wiki Notes allow it at any time on the first floor.
decisions.note: Not on the chart; listed for its relationship change.

benchmark.note: Hub option, Alice +1, offered at any time on the first floor. Shown as the game’s label, TOY.

decisions.title: Ask to go upstairs
decisions.context: “I’ve made a good start down here. I’ll head upstairs!” Todd: “Do what you have to do, but stop bothering me!”
decisions.note: Chart node on the line leaving the bracket.

benchmark.note: The hub’s exit option; requires the trash.

decisions.title: Go Upstairs (checkpoint)
decisions.context: Kara goes up. Urgent: tidy Todd’s room, tidy Alice’s room. Optional: clean bathroom, clean restroom.
decisions.note: Chart checkpoint.

benchmark.note: A narrated event with a single Continue.

decisions.title: Clean Todd’s room; Alice goes to her room
decisions.context: Make the bed, clear the mess, open his window. While Kara makes the bed, Alice goes to her room (triangle event). An ad for a child android model falls out of his bills. Leaving, Todd shoves Kara out of the restroom: “Watch it!”
decisions.note: Two chart nodes.

benchmark.note: Hub option; Alice is in her room from then on (the book’s increase and the talk need her there).

decisions.title: Tidy pills; Kara sees gun
decisions.context: Antidepressants on the nightstand (“Contains Tianeptine / Risk of behavioral disorders”); putting them in the drawer reveals a gun.

options.label: TIDY PILLS → KARA SEES GUN
options.effect: Unlock: “Gun accessible in Stormy Night and Fugitives”.

decisions.note: Yellow unlock node (open padlock).

benchmark.note: Hub option after Todd’s room; the only thing that sets gunDiscovered.

decisions.title: Clean toilet
decisions.context: The restroom across from Todd’s room, after Todd leaves it.
decisions.note: Chart node (objective CLEAN RESTROOM).

benchmark.note: Hub option after Todd’s room (the transcript’s order; the wiki says after either bedroom).

decisions.title: Clean bathroom
decisions.context: Arrange bottles, store dirty clothes, mop the floor.
decisions.note: Chart node. PowerPyx says it is needed before the Alice talk; the transcript marks it optional.

benchmark.note: Hub option, not required for the talk.

decisions.title: Read the magazine in Todd’s room
decisions.context: A magazine with two covers on the cupboard by Todd’s door; the bedroom TV plays sports, job losses and President Warren’s 200,000 android combat units.

options.label: READ “ANDROID QB”
options.effect: All Sports: CyberLife’s QB1000 quarterback demo.

options.label: READ “PUTTING A PRICE”
options.effect: Tech Addict, “The Price of Life”: driverless cars assign victims a value.

options.label: Watch TV (not a chart node)
options.effect: Sports, 225,000 jobs lost and 37.3% unemployment, the President’s android army order.

decisions.gate: Optional, in Todd’s room, also after the talk.
decisions.note: Two optional chart nodes; the TV is not on the chart. No public-opinion effect.

benchmark.note: A media scene after the talk (“Back In Hallway”), with the TV as a third item.

decisions.title: Clean Alice’s room
decisions.context: Make Alice’s bed (“I only need two minutes. Is that okay, Alice?” if she is there).
decisions.note: Chart node.

benchmark.note: Hub option; its text depends on whether Alice is already in her room.

decisions.title: Ventilate room; Kara discovers a way down
decisions.context: Kara opens Alice’s window as part of tidying her room and finds a roof edge. The operator confirmed in game (2026-11-07) that the window cannot be skipped; the benchmark bundles it into the tidy action since story 1.9.5.

options.label: VENTILATE ROOM → KARA DISCOVERS A WAY DOWN

decisions.note: Yellow unlock node (open padlock). Whether the room can be finished with the window shut is an open question.

benchmark.note: Hub option after Alice’s room; the only thing that sets the new window flag. Stormy Night does not read it yet.

decisions.title: The Alice in Wonderland book (not a chart node)
decisions.context: The book on Alice’s floor. “Alice In Wonderland… Of course.” Alice smiles.

options.label: Look at it with Alice there
options.effect: Alice up: “Looking at the Alice in Wonderland book in her room ↑”. Zlatko: “Recall Alice’s Book”.

options.label: Look at it without Alice
options.effect: No change (wiki Notes); still seen for Zlatko.

decisions.note: Not on the chart; a cross-chapter impact in the wiki’s list.

benchmark.note: Two variants of one hub option; +1 only once Alice is in her room. The title is rendered with the girl’s name token.

decisions.title: Talk with Alice (her room)
decisions.context: Four menus (transcript): FACTUAL / FRIENDLY / DIPLOMATIC; then NAME KARA / INTERESTS? / SEEM QUIET / MOTHER?; then the three not said; then the two left plus LEAVE ALONE.

options.label: MOTHER
options.effect: Alice down: the chapter’s only decrease.

options.label: FACTUAL, SEEM QUIET, LEAVE ALONE
options.effect: No change (LEAVE ALONE only in the fourth menu). Once SEEM QUIET is said the third menu has only lines with arrows.

decisions.note: Chart node TALK WITH ALICE (speech bubble), leaving the bracket.

benchmark.note: The second-floor hub’s exit, then four dialogue scenes (story 1.9.1 had three, with LEAVE ALONE in the third). Options show the game’s labels (FACTUAL, FRIENDLY, DIPLOMATIC; NAME KARA, INTERESTS?, SEEM QUIET, MOTHER?, LEAVE ALONE); SEEM QUIET has no arrow in the game’s text.

decisions.title: Alice gives Kara a key
decisions.context: Alice leaves; she gives Kara a key “if Alice has at least Neutral status”, otherwise “Alice coldly runs off”.
decisions.note: Triangle event node.

benchmark.note: Automatic at the end of the fourth menu (K01g2): the key at the lowest bond the Alice scale calls Neutral (ALICE_KEY, 2 points); an event scene when given.

decisions.title: Open Alice’s box
decisions.context: A clover, a photo of Todd, his wife and his biological daughter, and Alice’s drawings: the mother, Todd and his wife, Kara examined, Kara broken.

options.label: OPEN ALICE’S BOX
options.effect: “Allows you to persuade Todd if he’s alive in Battle for Detroit”; the Todd page says the family photo is what matters.

decisions.note: Drawn blue with no padlock, although the wiki lists it as a cross-chapter impact.

benchmark.note: A decision scene offered only with the key; opening it sets aliceBox.

decisions.title: Finished Cleaning (ending)
decisions.context: Downstairs, Todd rages at Alice (“SAY IT! YOU HATE ME!”), grabs her, then breaks down and apologizes.

options.label: FINISHED CLEANING
options.effect: The chapter’s only ending, on every path.

decisions.note: Ending card, no icon.

benchmark.note: A narrated event; the table is clear or not depending on the dishes.
